title: Tecolutla Formation Tops.csv
doc_date: undated; Drive modified 2019-01-27 (same day as the header, perforation and survey CSVs)
issuer_author: not stated (Tonalli project export; values match the GLJ 2019 top-El-Abra map labels)
summary: Measured-depth tops for 9 wells: three Tantoyuca columns, top El Abra, O/W contact, and an "EL_ABRA_HZ_L" column. No TVD/SS, no interpreter, no date inside the file.
interpretation: Converted with header-CSV KBs (vertical wells) or the repo survey-based mSS (TEC-10, TEC-11): top El Abra TEC-6 -2,294.1, TEC-2 -2,301.6, TEC-7 -2,304.0, TEC-10 -2,309.7, TEC-11DES -2,311.9, TEC-101 -2,333.7, TEC-3 -2,372.6, TEC-5 -2,551.0 mSS. These reproduce the GLJ 2019 map labels to <=0.3 m, so this file is the source of the GLJ tops. O/W contact: TEC-3 -2,374.0 mSS (= GLJ LKO -2,374.2, set at TEC-3 TD) and TEC-10 -2,402.8 mSS (coincides with the base of perforation zone A 2,433.5-2,442.5 mMD, which gave no inflow and was tight on the 2018 injectivity test, i.e. not a tested contact). TEC-11DES El Abra pick (2,611.8 mMD, -2,311.9 mSS) is 252 m MD / 66 m TVD below the carbonate onset in the Rise mud log (2,360 mMD, -2,245 mSS), which this file calls Tantoyuca_A (2,356.55 mMD); TEC-11 lithology and this pick disagree. Tantoyuca columns are internally inconsistent (TEC-3 and TEC-2 Tantoyuca_A shallower than Tantoyuca top) and differ from PEMEX Tantoyuca tops by up to 68 m (TEC-6 PEMEX 2,229 vs 2,160.75 mMD).
use_in_presentation: Structure/tops slide; OWC question (briefing Q2); TEC-12 window slide
repo_impact: adds+confirms: first printed tops for TEC-3 (-2,372.6 mSS), TEC-7 (-2,304.0) and TEC-11DES (-2,311.9) in the repo; confirms GLJ map tops and TEC-9 2,309.84 mMD; TEC-10 pick 2,344.58 mMD (-2,309.7 mSS) is 2.7 m deeper than the XS-panel 2,307 mSS used in G-47 update 2026-10-24; adds a 4th OWC value (TEC-10 -2,402.8 mSS) to briefing Q2; TEC-2 2,305.64 mMD contradicts the TAN "2,320 mMD/2,316 mSS" reading; TEC-11 pick contradicts mud-log lithology. G-47, G-46 (minor), geology notes item 4-5 (tops missing) partly closed.

folder_path: Geology/Tecolutla-10 Core and Sample Descriptions/Sample Descriptions/TEC-10 Rockwise XRD
title: 100851_Tonalli Energy_Tecolutla-10_RockWise Report_05028AM.xlsx
issuer_author: "Wellsite Geoscience Service" RockWise report no. 100851 for Tonalli Energia; primary contact Curtis Hess; WBM
summary: Bulk XRD (wt%) on 62 TEC-10 cutting samples 2,290-2,490 mMD (2 m spacing to 2,360, then 5 m) with a formation column (Tantoyuca / El Abra) and a brittleness index. Total clay only, no clay speciation; no TOC/pyrolysis despite template notes.
key_data_with_units: Tantoyuca 2,290-2,346 mMD (29 samples): quartz 22-40 %, K-spar 0-3 %, plagioclase 3-6 %, total clay 3-18 %, calcite 45-59 %, dolomite 0-4 %, pyrite 0-6 %. TEC-12 window at TEC-10 (2,328-2,346 mMD = 2,294-2,311 mSS, 10 samples): quartz mean 31.3 % (26-40), Q+F mean 37.6 % (31-47), clay mean 9.0 % (3-16), calcite mean 49.5 % (45-55), dolomite 0.7 % (0-2), pyrite mean 3.2 % (0-6; 4-6 % at 2,336-2,346). El Abra from 2,348 mMD (-2,312.9 mSS): calcite 91 % with 3 % quartz and 4 % clay at 2,348, then calcite 92-100 %, dolomite 0-6 % (6 % at 2,358), quartz/clay trace. Perforated interval samples 2,350/2,352 mMD: calcite 97/98 %, quartz 2 %, clay trace.
interpretation: Formation boundary between 2,346 and 2,348 mMD (2,311.0-2,312.9 mSS on the survey basis), matching the log GR drop (82 to 36 gAPI) and resistivity rise (9 to 19-29 ohm.m) at 2,345-2,346 mMD and the tops-file pick 2,344.58 mMD. The whole TEC-12 window at TEC-10 is therefore Tantoyuca: a silty/sandy calcareous marl with ~30-40 % quartz-feldspar and ~9 % clay, not El Abra reef limestone. The window's PE 3.8 is explained by quartz+clay diluting calcite, not by dolomite (dolomite <=2 %); a rough mass-weighted PE from the XRD at 2,330 mMD gives ~3.7 b/e (my estimate). 4-6 % pyrite at 2,336-2,346 mMD may further depress induction resistivity. The TEC-10 "window water-saturated" result (Sw>=1.1) is a Tantoyuca result and says nothing about El Abra saturation in the crestal window. Caveats: cuttings (lag/caving), 2 m sampling, bulk clay only.
use_in_presentation: TEC-12 window / G-47 slide (lead item); petrophysics backup; answer to "why was the upper zone not perforated"
repo_impact: corrects+confirms G-47: confirms and sharpens the 2026-10-24 update (window above top El Abra at TEC-10) - not 13-16 m but the full 17 m of the window is Tantoyuca at TEC-10; corrects "argillaceous/dolomitic" (no dolomite); fills the "no XRD/mineralogy" gap in fluids_rock_core_notes.md item 7 (for cuttings); partially contradicts docs/09 sec 2 and briefing A7 "GR polarity confirmed field-wide": at TEC-10 the rho(GR,neutron)=0.28 comes from Tantoyuca (0.71); inside El Abra only it is -0.20 (density -0.40) per my recomputation from TEC10_logs_mss.csv (TEC-9 0.45 and TEC-2 0.34 hold within El Abra).
